* Compute dispatches use work groups that are a multiple of warp size.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of warps that require more than 32 registers.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every warp that requires more than 32 registers. Threads which require more than 32 registers consume two thread slots in the register file, halving the number of threads that can be concurrently active in the shader core.
Reduction in thread count can impact the ability of the shader core to keep functional units busy, and means that performance is more likely to be impacted by stalls caused by cache misses.
Aim to minimize the number of threads requiring more than 32 registers, by using simpler shader programs and lower precision data types.

groups.name: Shader Threads
groups.longDescription:
This counter group shows the number of threads created, split by type. This can help you to understand the running workload mix.
Counters in this group are derived by scaling quad or warp counters, and their counts include unused thread slots in the coarser granule.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of non-fragment threads started.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the number of non-fragment threads started.
The expression is an approximation, based on the assumption that all warps are fully populated with threads. The {{C::MaliCoreFullWarp}} counter can give some indication of warp occupancy.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of fragment threads started.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the number of fragment threads started. This counter assumes all 4 lanes in a coarse quad are active, so this counter includes helper threads and idle thread slots if a coarse quad has partial coverage.

groups.name: Shader Workload Properties
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows interesting properties of the running shader code, most of which highlight an interesting optimization opportunity.

metrics.shortDescription: The thread occupancy of the fragment warps.
metrics.longDescription: This expression measures the thread occupancy of the fragment warps in percent. Threads are counted as active if they are part of a coarse quad, even if they have no sample coverage.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage of warps that have a full thread slot allocation.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the percentage of warps that have a full thread slot allocation. Note that allocated thread slots might not contain a running thread if the workload can not fill the whole allocation.
If a high percentage of warps are not fully allocated then performance is reduced. Fully allocated warps are more likely if:
* Draw calls avoid late ZS dependency hazards.
* Draw calls use meshes with a low percentage of tiny primitives.
* Compute dispatches use work groups that are a multiple of warp size.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage of warps that require more than 32 registers.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the percentage of warps that use more than 32 registers, requiring the full register allocation of 64 registers. Warps that require more than 32 registers halve the peak thread occupancy of the shader core, and can make shader performance more sensitive to cache misses and memory stalls.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage of instructions that have control flow divergence across the warp.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the percentage of instructions that have control flow divergence across the warp.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage of arithmetic instructions that operate on 8/16-bit types.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the percentage of arithmetic instructions that operate on 8/16-bit types. These are more energy efficient, and require fewer registers for variable storage, than 32-bit operations.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage of fragments that use shader-based blending.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the percentage of fragments that use shader-based blending, rather than the fixed-function blend path. These fragments are caused by the application using color formats, or advanced blend equations, which the fixed-function blend path does not support.
Vulkan shaders that use software blending do not show up in this data, because the blend is inlined into the main body of the shader program.

sections.name: Shader Core Arithmetic Unit
sections.longDescription:
The arithmetic unit in the shader core processes all the arithmetic and logic operations in the running shader programs.
Performance counters in this section show how the running programs use the arithmetic units, which may indicate the type of operations that are consuming the most performance.

groups.name: ALU Cycles
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of cycles when work is issued to the arithmetic and logic unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the arithmetic unit is busy.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the number of cycles that the arithmetic unit is busy processing work.

groups.name: Instruction Cache
groups.longDescription: This counter group monitors the behavior of the instruction cache.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of instruction cache misses.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every instruction cache miss.
Note that the instruction cache is shared across both processing units. Unlike most processing unit counters this counter increments for cache misses from both units.

groups.name: ALU Instructions
groups.longDescription: This counter group gives a breakdown of the types of arithmetic instructions being used by the shader program.

metrics.shortDescription: The total number of instructions issued to the FMA, CVT, and SFU pipes.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the number of total instructions issued to any of the arithmetic pipe types.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of instructions issued to the FMA pipe.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every instruction issued to the fused multiply-accumulate pipe.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of instructions issued to the CVT pipe.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every instruction issued to the convert pipe.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of instructions issued to the SFU pipe.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every instruction issued to the special functions unit pipe.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of instructions run per warp that have control flow divergence.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every instruction the programmable core processes per warp when there is control flow divergence across the warp. Control flow divergence erodes arithmetic processing efficiency because it implies some threads in the warp are idle because they do not take the current control path through the code. Aim to minimize control flow divergence when designing shader effects.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of narrow arithmetic instructions.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every instruction that does 16-bit or narrower calculations.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of blend shader invocations run.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every blend shader invocation run.
This counter increments per fetch unit, and so can increase by up to 4 in a clock cycle.

groups.name: ALU Utilization
groups.longDescription:
This counter group gives a breakdown of the usage of the different arithmetic sub-units, relative to their speed-of-light performance.
Due to shared issue data paths, it might not be possible for individual ALU units to reach their speed-of-light if the other ALU hardware units are also in use.

metrics.shortDescription: The utilization of the FMA pipes.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the fused multiply-accumulate pipeline utilization.
This pipeline shares instruction issue slots with CVT and SFU instructions, so it is not possible to achieve 100% utilization unless the other pipelines are idle.

metrics.shortDescription: Defines the utilization of the CVT pipe.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the convert pipeline utilization.
This pipeline shares instruction issue slots with FMA and SFU instructions, so it is not possible to achieve 100% utilization unless the other pipelines are idle.

metrics.shortDescription: The utilization of the SFU pipe.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the special functions unit pipeline utilization.
This pipeline shares instruction issue slots with CVT and SFU instructions, so it is not possible to achieve 100% utilization unless the other pipelines are idle.

sections.name: Shader Core Load/store Unit
sections.longDescription:
The load/store unit in the shader core handles all generic read/write data access, including access to vertex attributes, buffers, images, workgroup local storage, and the program stack.
Performance counters in this section show a breakdown of load/store cache accesses, showing whether accesses use an entire cache line or only part of one.

groups.name: Load/Store Unit Cycles
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of cycles when work is issued to the load/store unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The total number of load/store issue cycles.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of load/store cache access cycles. This counter ignores secondary effects such as cache misses, so provides the minimum possible cycle usage.

metrics.shortDescription: The total number of load/store read cycles.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of load/store read cycles.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of full-width load/store cache reads.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every full-width load/store cache read.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of partial-width load/store cache reads.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every partial-width load/store cache read. Partial data accesses do not make full use of the load/store cache capability. Merging short accesses together to make fewer larger requests improves efficiency. To do this in shader code:
* Use vector data loads.
* Avoid padding in strided data accesses.
* Write compute shaders so that adjacent threads in a warp access adjacent addresses in memory.

metrics.shortDescription: The total number of load/store write cycles.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of load/store write cycles.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of full-width load/store cache writes.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every full-width load/store cache write.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of partial-width load/store cache writes.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every partial-width load/store cache write. Partial data accesses do not make full use of the load/store cache capability. Merging short accesses together to make fewer larger requests improves efficiency. To do this in shader code:
* Use vector data loads.
* Avoid padding in strided data accesses.
* Write compute shaders so that adjacent threads in a warp access adjacent addresses in memory.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of load/store atomic accesses.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every atomic access.
Atomic memory accesses are typically multicycle operations per thread in the warp, so they are exceptionally expensive. Minimize the use of atomics in performance critical code. For some types of atomic operation, it can be beneficial to perform a warp-wide reduction using subgroup operations and then use a single thread to update the atomic value.

sections.name: Shader Core Varying Unit
sections.longDescription:
The varying unit in the shader core handles all vertex data interpolation in fragment shaders.
Performance counters in this section show a breakdown of interpolation operations.

groups.name: Varying Unit Requests
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of requests made to the varying interpolation unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of warp-width interpolation operations processed by the varying unit.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every warp-width interpolation operation processed by the varying unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of 16-bit interpolation slot issues to the varying unit.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every 16-bit per component interpolation slot issued to the varying unit.
The number of threads per slot, the number of components per slot, and the number of slot issues per cycle, is implementation dependent.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of 32-bit interpolation slot issues to the varying unit.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every 32-bit per component interpolation slot issued to the varying unit. 32-bit interpolation is half the performance of 16-bit interpolation, so if content is varying bound consider reducing precision of varying inputs to fragment shaders.
The number of threads per slot, the number of components per slot, and the number of slot issues per cycle, is implementation dependent.

groups.name: Varying Unit Cycles
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of cycles when work is issued to the varying interpolation unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The total number of varying unit issue cycles.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of cycles when the varying interpolator is issuing operations.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of 16-bit interpolation cycles used by the varying unit.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every 16-bit per component interpolation cycle processed by the varying unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of 32-bit interpolation cycles used by the varying unit.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every 32-bit per component interpolation cycle processed by the varying unit. 32-bit interpolation is half the performance of 16-bit interpolation, so if content is varying bound consider reducing precision of varying inputs to fragment shaders.

sections.name: Shader Core Texture Unit
sections.longDescription:
The texture unit in the shader core handles all read-only texture access and filtering.
Performance counters in this section show a breakdown of texturing operations and the use of sub-units inside the texturing hardware.

groups.name: Texture Unit Requests
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of requests made to the texture unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of texture samples made.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the number of texture samples made.

groups.name: Texture Unit Quads
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of fragment quads submitted to the texture unit for sampling.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of quad-width texture operations processed by the texture unit.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every quad-width texture operation processed by the texture unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of output texture messages from the texture unit.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every texture message emitted by the texture unit.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit messages with single quad
metrics.shortDescription: The number of single quad output texture messages from the texture unit.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every texture message emitted by the texture unit which only contains a single quad.

groups.name: Texture Unit Cycles
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of cycles when work is issued to the sub-units inside the texture unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the texture unit is active.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every clock cycle when the texture unit is active, and contains an active sample message.
A high active time does not imply a high utilization. The unit counts as active even if only a single pipeline stage is busy.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the texture unit is busy.
metrics.longDescription: This expression measures the number of cycles the texture unit is busy processing work.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles computing texel index values.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every clock cycle when the texture unit is computing a texel index value.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of texture filtering issue cycles.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every texture filtering issue cycle. This GPU can do {{C::MaliTexSamplePerCy.equation}}x 2D bilinear texture samples per clock. More complex filtering operations are composed of multiple 2D bilinear samples, and take proportionally more filtering time to complete. The scaling factors for more expensive operations are:
* 2D trilinear filtering runs at half speed.
* 3D bilinear filtering runs at half speed.
* 3D trilinear filtering runs at quarter speed.
Anisotropic filtering makes up to MAX_ANISOTROPY filtered subsamples of the current base filter type. For example, using trilinear filtering with a MAX_ANISOTROPY of 3 will require up to 6 bilinear filters.

groups.name: Texture Unit Stall Cycles
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of stall cycles when work can not be issued to the sub-units inside the texture unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the texture unit is active but does not return a texture sample.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every clock cycle when the texture unit is active and a response message can be accepted, but no response is generated.
A high value here can be indicative of inefficient texturing operations that are failing to sustain full throughput, and can be caused by a high miss rate in either the descriptor or data cache, or complex multicycle filtering operations.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when a quad is stalled on texture descriptor fetch.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every clock cycle a quad is stalled on texture descriptor fetch. This might not correspond to a stall cycle in the filtering unit if there is enough work already buffered after the descriptor fetcher to hide the stall.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit data fetch stall cycles
metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when a quad is stalled on entering texture fetch because the fetch queue is full.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every clock cycle a quad is stalled on entering texture fetch because the fetch queue is full. This might not correspond to a stall cycle in the filtering unit if there is enough work already buffered to hide the stall.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the filtering unit is idle and there is at least one quad present in the texture data fetch queue.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every clock cycle the filtering unit is idle and there is at least one quad present in the texture data fetch queue. A high stall rate here can be indicative of content which is failing to make good use of the texture cache. For example, under-sampling from a high resolution texture.

groups.name: Texture Unit CPI
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the average cost of texture samples.

metrics.shortDescription: The average number of texture filtering cycles per instruction.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the average number of texture filtering cycles per instruction. For texture-limited content that has a CPI higher than the optimal throughout of this core ({{C::MaliTexSamplePerCy.equation}} samples per cycle), consider using simpler texture filters. See {{C::MaliTexIssueCy}} for details of the expected performance for different types of operation.

groups.name: Texture Unit Utilization
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the use of some of the functional units and data paths inside the texture unit, relative to their speed-of-light capability.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage utilization of the texture message input bus.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the percentage utilization of the texture message input bus.
If bus utilization is higher than the filtering unit utilization, your content might be limited by texture operation parameter passing. Requests that require more input parameters, such as 3D accesses, array accesses, and accesses using an explicit level-of-detail, place a higher load on the bus than basic 2D texture operations.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage utilization of the texturing cache lookup unit.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the percentage utilization of the texture cache lookup unit.
If cache lookup unit utilization is high, relative to other texture unit component utilization, you might be able to reduce texturing cost by using narrower texture color formats. For ASTC textures you can narrow the post-decompression format by using the decode_mode extensions.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage utilization of the texture filtering unit.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the percentage utilization of the texture filtering unit.
If filtering unit utilization is high, relative to other texture unit component utilization, you might be able to reduce texturing cost by using simpler texture filters. You can do this by using less trilinear filtering and anisotropic filtering.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage utilization of the texture message output bus.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the percentage utilization of the texture message output bus.
If bus utilization is higher than the filtering unit utilization, your content might be limited by texture result return. Requests that require higher precision sampler return type place a higher load on the bus, so it is recommended to use a 16-bit sampler precision whenever possible.

groups.name: Texture Unit Cache Cycles
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of cache access cycles for the data caches inside the texture unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles returning data from the texture cache.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every clock cycle when the texture cache is returning data.
A high value here can be indicative of an inefficient post-decompression texture format. For example, a 64-bpp format takes twice as long to read as a 32-bpp format.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit L1 texture cache load cycles
metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles loading data into the L1 texture cache.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every clock cycle when data is being transferred into the L1 texture cache.
A high value here can be indicative of a high cache miss rate in the texture data cache.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit L1 texture cache lookup cycles
metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles accessing the L1 texture cache.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every clock cycle when the L1 texture cache is being accessed.
A high value here can be indicative of a high cache miss rate in the texture data cache.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit L1 texture cache output cycles
metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles returning data from the L1 texture cache.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every clock cycle when the L1 texture cache is returning data for a sampling operation.
A high value here can be indicative of a high cache miss rate in the texture data cache.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit simple texture load cycles
metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles loading simple texture formats.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every clock cycle when the texture cache is fetching formats with simple data layouts using the direct path.
A high value here can be indicative of a high cache miss rate in the texture data cache.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit complex texture load cycles
metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles loading complex texture formats.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every clock cycle when the texture cache is fetching formats with complex data layouts using the decompressor path.
A high value here can be indicative of a high cache miss rate in the texture data cache.

groups.name: Texture Unit Bus
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of bus cycles used on the texture unit memory bus connecting the texture unit to the rest of the shader core.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of texture request message data beats.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every clock cycle of input request data sent to the texture unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of texture response message data beats.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every clock cycle of output response data sent by the texture unit.

sections.name: Shader Core Ray Tracing Unit
sections.longDescription:
The ray tracing unit in the shader core handles hardware accelerated bounding box and triangle intersection testing.
Performance counters in this section show a breakdown of intersection tests and the use of sub-units inside the ray tracing unit.

groups.name: Ray Tracing Unit Cycles
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of cycles when work is issued to the ray tracing unit and the various sub-units inside it.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the ray tracing unit is issuing work.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of cycles when the ray tracing unit is issuing work to a functional unit.

metrics.humanName: Ray tracing box tester issue cycles
metrics.shortDescription: The number of active issue cycles for the ray tracing box test unit.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every clock cycle the ray tracing unit issues a box intersection operation. If this counter is a high percentage of shader core active, then shader performance might be limited by acceleration structure traversal.
The main workload for ray tracing is traversing the acceleration structure so this counter is expected to be high. If the counter is not high, and a significant number of rays are being used, it indicates that a bottleneck exists elsewhere.

metrics.humanName: Ray tracing triangle tester issue cycles
metrics.shortDescription: The number of active issue cycles for the ray tracing triangle test unit.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every clock cycle the ray tracing unit issues a triangle intersection test. If this counter is a high percentage of shader core active, then shader performance might be limited by triangle testing.
A good acceleration structure culls most triangles using box tests higher up the tree, so that rays do not need to be tested against them. If this counter is high it might indicate an issue with either geometry complexity or acceleration structure efficiency.

groups.name: Ray Tracing Unit Rays
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of rays processed by the ray tracing unit, including a breakdown of any interesting ray properties.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of rays started.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every ray that is started and tested against the root node in the acceleration structure.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of rays that terminate on their first hit.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every ray that terminates on its first triangle hit. Rays that terminate on first hit are more efficient to process, as they do not need to keep testing to find the closest hit.
First-hit tests are well suited to techniques that determine occlusion, such as shadow mapping. In these use cases you don't need to know which object is hit, just that an object is hit between the ray source and destination.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of triangle intersection tests that do not intersect.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every ray-triangle intersection test that does not intersect the triangle.
Most triangles that a ray misses are expected to be culled by box tests during acceleration structure traversal, so if rays are triggering a high number of triangle intersection tests, try improving the acceleration structure quality.
A high number for this counter might also indicate a programming error, such as using opaque triangles and requesting that opaque hits be culled.

groups.name: Ray Tracing Unit Triangle Tests
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the histogram of triangle test unit occupancy, which schedules tests on warp-width vectors. Warps with divergent rays result in tests with a subset of lanes active, which reduces efficiency.

metrics.humanName: Ray tracing triangle nodes with 1-4 rays
metrics.shortDescription: The number of triangle nodes with 1 to 4 active rays in the warp.
metrics.longDescription: This count increments for every triangle node tested when there are between 1 and 4 active rays in the warp. A high percentage of tests with low warp occupancy can indicate an issue with ray coherency. Try to group rays with similar origin, direction, and range together.

metrics.humanName: Ray tracing triangle nodes with 5-8 rays
metrics.shortDescription: The number of triangle nodes with 5 to 8 active rays in the warp.
metrics.longDescription: This count increments for every triangle node tested when there are between 5 and 8 active rays in the warp. A high percentage of tests with low warp occupancy can indicate an issue with ray coherency. Try to group rays with similar origin, direction, and range together.

metrics.humanName: Ray tracing triangle nodes with 9-12 rays
metrics.shortDescription: The number of triangle nodes with 9 to 12 active rays in the warp.
metrics.longDescription: This count increments for every triangle node tested when there are between 9 and 12 active rays in the warp. A high percentage of tests with low warp occupancy can indicate an issue with ray coherency. Try to group rays with similar origin, direction, and range together.

metrics.humanName: Ray tracing triangle nodes with 13-16 rays
metrics.shortDescription: The number of triangle nodes with 13 to 16 active rays in the warp.
metrics.longDescription: This count increments for every triangle node tested when there are between 13 and 16 active rays in the warp.

groups.name: Ray Tracing Unit Box Tests
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the histogram of bounding box test unit occupancy, which schedules tests on warp-width vectors. Warps with divergent rays result in tests with a subset of lanes active, which reduces efficiency.

metrics.humanName: Ray tracing box nodes with 1-4 rays
metrics.shortDescription: The number of acceleration structure box nodes with 1 to 4 active rays in the warp.
metrics.longDescription: This count increments for every acceleration structure box node tested when there are between 1 and 4 active rays in the warp. A high percentage of tests with low warp occupancy can indicate an issue with ray coherency. Try to group rays with similar origin, direction, and range together.

metrics.humanName: Ray tracing box nodes with 5-8 rays
metrics.shortDescription: The number of acceleration structure box nodes with 5 to 8 active rays in the warp.
metrics.longDescription: This count increments for every acceleration structure box node tested when there are between 5 and 8 active rays in the warp. A high percentage of tests with low warp occupancy can indicate an issue with ray coherency. Try to group rays with similar origin, direction, and range together.

metrics.humanName: Ray tracing box nodes with 9-12 rays
metrics.shortDescription: The number of acceleration structure box nodes with 9 to 12 active rays in the warp.
metrics.longDescription: This count increments for every acceleration structure box node tested when there are between 9 and 12 active rays in the warp. A high percentage of tests with low warp occupancy can indicate an issue with ray coherency. Try to group rays with similar origin, direction, and range together.

metrics.humanName: Ray tracing box nodes with 13-16 rays
metrics.shortDescription: The number of acceleration structure box nodes with 13 to 16 active rays in the warp.
metrics.longDescription: This count increments for every acceleration structure box node tested when there are between 13 and 16 active rays in the warp.

groups.name: Ray Tracing Unit Box Workload
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of bounding box tests processed by the box test unit, including the split between TLAS and BLAS box tests.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of acceleration structure bounding boxes tested.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every acceleration structure bounding box node tested. If this value is high then the ray tracing unit spends a lot of time traversing the acceleration structure. High node counts, acceleration structure inefficiency, and ray divergence across a warp can all cause the counter value to be high.
Nodes have a variable duration that depends on the number of bounding boxes they contain, and the number of active rays in each warp.

groups.name: Ray Tracing Unit Triangle Workload
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of triangles processed by the triangle test unit, including key properties of the triangles.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of opaque triangle hits.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every ray intersection with an opaque triangle.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of non-opaque triangle hits.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every ray intersection with a non-opaque triangle.
Non-opaque triangles are more expensive to process than opaque triangles, so Arm recommends using opaque triangles in acceleration structures.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of triangle nodes tested.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every triangle node tested. If this value is high then the ray tracing unit spends a lot of time testing for intersection with triangles, and can be caused by high triangle counts, acceleration structure inefficiency, and ray divergence across a warp.
Nodes have a variable duration that depends on the number of triangles they contain, and the number of active rays in each warp.

sections.name: Shader Core Other Units
sections.longDescription:
In addition to the main units, covered in earlier sections, the shader core has several other units that can be measured.
Performance counters in this section show the workload on these other units.

groups.name: Attribute Unit Requests
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of requests made to the attribute unit.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of instructions run by the attribute unit.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every instruction run by the attribute unit.
Each instruction converts a logical attribute access into a pointer-based access, which is then processed by the load/store unit.

sections.name: Shader Core Memory Access
sections.longDescription:
GPUs are data-plane processors, so understanding your memory bandwidth and where it is coming from is a critical piece of knowledge when trying to improve performance.
Performance counters in this section show the breakdown of memory accesses by shader core hardware unit, showing the total amount of read and write bandwidth being generated by the shader core.
Read bandwidth is split to show how much is provided by the GPU L2 cache and how much is provided by the external memory system. Write bandwidth does not have an equivalent split, and it is not possible to tell from the counters if a write goes to L2 or directly to external memory.

groups.name: Shader Core L2 Reads
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of shader core read transactions served from the L2 cache, broken down by hardware unit inside the shader core.

metrics.humanName: Fragment front-end read beats from L2 cache
metrics.shortDescription: The number of read beats received by the fixed-function fragment front-end.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read beat received by the fixed-function fragment front-end.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit read beats from L2 cache
metrics.shortDescription: The number of read beats received by the load/store unit.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read beat received by the load/store unit.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit read beats from L2 cache
metrics.shortDescription: The number of read beats received by the texture unit.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read beat received by the texture unit.

metrics.humanName: Other shader core read beats from L2 cache
metrics.shortDescription: The number of read beats received by a unit not specifically identified.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read beat received by any unit that is not identified as a specific data destination.

groups.name: Shader Core External Reads
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of shader core read transactions served from external memory, broken down by hardware unit inside the shader core.

metrics.humanName: Fragment front-end read beats from external memory
metrics.shortDescription: The number of read beats received by the fixed-function fragment front-end that require an external memory access due to an L2 cache miss.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read beat received by the fixed-function fragment front-end that requires an external memory access due to an L2 cache miss.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit read beats from external memory
metrics.shortDescription: The number of read beats received by the load/store unit that require an external memory access due to an L2 cache miss.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read beat received by the load/store unit that requires an external memory access due to an L2 cache miss.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit read beats from external memory
metrics.shortDescription: The number of read beats received by the texture unit that require an external memory access due to an L2 cache miss.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read beat received by the texture unit that requires an external memory access due to an L2 cache miss.

groups.name: Shader Core L2 Writes
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of shader core write transactions, broken down by hardware unit inside the shader core.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit write beats to L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The number of write beats sent by the load/store unit.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every write beat sent by the load/store unit.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit write-back write beats to L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The number of write beats by the load/store unit that are caused by write-back.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every write beat by the load/store unit that is caused by write-back.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit other write beats to L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The number of write beats by the load/store unit that are not caused by write-back.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every write beat by the load/store unit that is not caused by write-back.

metrics.humanName: Tile unit write beats to L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The number of write beats sent by the framebuffer tile write-back unit.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every write beat sent by the framebuffer tile write-back unit.

groups.name: Shader Core L2 Read Bytes
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of bytes read from the L2 cache by the shader core, broken down by hardware unit inside the shader core.

metrics.humanName: Fragment front-end read bytes from L2 cache
metrics.shortDescription: The total number of bytes read from the L2 memory system by the shader core fragment front-end.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of bytes read from the L2 memory system by the fragment front-end.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit read bytes from L2 cache
metrics.shortDescription: The total number of bytes read from the L2 memory system by the load/store unit.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of bytes read from the L2 memory system by the load/store unit.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit read bytes from L2 cache
metrics.shortDescription: The total number of bytes read from the L2 memory system by the texture unit.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of bytes read from the L2 memory system by the texture unit.

metrics.humanName: Other shader core read bytes from L2 cache
metrics.shortDescription: The number of read bytes received by a unit not specifically identified.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read byte received by any unit that is not identified as a specific data destination.

groups.name: Shader Core External Read Bytes
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of bytes read from external memory by the shader core, broken down by hardware unit inside the shader core.

metrics.humanName: Fragment front-end read bytes from external memory
metrics.shortDescription: The total number of bytes read from the external memory system by the shader core fragment front-end.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of bytes read from the external memory system by the fragment front-end.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit read bytes from external memory
metrics.shortDescription: The total number of bytes read from the external memory system by the load/store unit.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of bytes read from the external memory system by the load/store unit.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit read bytes from external memory
metrics.shortDescription: The total number of bytes read from the external memory system by the texture unit.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of bytes read from the external memory system by the texture unit.

groups.name: Shader Core L2 Write Bytes
groups.longDescription:
This counter group shows the number of bytes written by the shader core, broken down by hardware unit inside the shader core.
These writes go to the L2 memory system, but counters can not determine if each write goes to the L2 cache or directly to external memory.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit write bytes to L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The total number of bytes written to the L2 memory system by the load/store unit.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of bytes written to the L2 memory system by the load/store unit.

metrics.humanName: Tile unit write bytes to L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The total number of bytes written to the L2 memory system by the framebuffer tile write-back unit.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the total number of bytes written to the L2 memory system by the framebuffer tile write-back unit.

groups.name: Load/Store Unit Bytes/Cycle
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of bytes accessed in the L2 cache and external memory per load/store cache access cycle. This gives some measure of how effectively the GPU is caching load/store data.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit bytes read from L2 per access cycle
metrics.shortDescription: The average number of bytes read from the L2 memory system by the load/store unit per read cycle.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the average number of bytes read from the L2 memory system by the load/store unit per read cycle. This metric gives some idea how effectively data is being cached in the L1 load/store cache.
If more bytes are being requested per access than you would expect for the data layout you are using, review your data layout and access patterns.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit bytes written to L2 per access cycle
metrics.shortDescription: The average number of bytes written to the L2 memory system by the load/store unit per write cycle.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the average number of bytes written to the L2 memory system by the load/store unit per write cycle.
If more bytes are being written per access than you would expect for the data layout you are using, review your data layout and access patterns to improve cache locality.

metrics.humanName: Load/store unit bytes read from external memory per access cycle
metrics.shortDescription: The average number of bytes read from the external memory system by the load/store unit per read cycle.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the average number of bytes read from the external memory system by the load/store unit per read cycle. This metric indicates how effectively data is being cached in the L2 cache.
If more bytes are being requested per access than you would expect for the data layout you are using, review your data layout and access patterns.

groups.name: Texture Unit Bytes/Cycle
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of bytes accessed in the L2 cache and external memory per texture sample. This gives some measure of how effectively the GPU is caching texture data.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit bytes read from L2 per texture cycle
metrics.shortDescription: The average number of bytes read from the L2 memory system by the texture unit per filtering cycle.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the average number of bytes read from the L2 memory system by the texture unit per filtering cycle. This metric indicates how effectively textures are being cached in the L1 texture cache.
If more bytes are being requested per access than you would expect for the format you are using, review your texture settings. Arm recommends:
* Using mipmaps for offline generated textures.
* Using ASTC or ETC compression for offline generated textures.
* Replacing runtime framebuffer formats with narrower formats.
* Reducing use of imageLoad/Store to allow framebuffer compression.
* Reducing use of negative LOD bias used for texture sharpening.
* Reducing use of anisotropic filtering, or reducing the level of MAX_ANISOTROPY used.

metrics.humanName: Texture unit bytes read from external memory per texture cycle
metrics.shortDescription: The average number of bytes read from the external memory system by the texture unit per filtering cycle.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the average number of bytes read from the external memory system by the texture unit per filtering cycle. This metric indicates how effectively textures are being cached in the L2 cache.
If more bytes are being requested per access than you would expect for the format you are using, review your texture settings. Arm recommends:
* Using mipmaps for offline generated textures.
* Using ASTC or ETC compression for offline generated textures.
* Replacing runtime framebuffer formats with narrower formats.
* Reducing use of imageLoad/Store to allow framebuffer compression.
* Reducing use of negative LOD bias used for texture sharpening.
* Reducing use of anisotropic filtering, or reducing the level of MAX_ANISOTROPY used.

groups.name: Tile Unit Bytes/Pixel
groups.longDescription:
This counter group shows the number of bytes written by the tile unit per output pixel. This can be used to determine the efficiency of application render pass store configuration.
Applications can minimize the number of bytes stored by following best practices:
* Use the smallest pixel color format that meets your requirements.
* Discard transient attachments that are no longer required at the end of each render pass (Vulkan storeOp=DONT_CARE or storeOp=NONE).
* Use resolve attachments to resolve multi-sampled data into a single value as part of tile write-back and discard the multi-sampled data so that it is not written back to memory.

metrics.humanName: Tile unit bytes written to L2 memory system per pixel
metrics.shortDescription: The average number of bytes written to the L2 memory system by the framebuffer tile unit per output pixel.
metrics.longDescription:
This expression defines the average number of bytes per output pixel written to the L2 memory system by the framebuffer tile unit.
If more bytes are being written per pixel than expected, Arm recommends:
* Using narrower attachment color formats with fewer bytes per pixel.
* Configuring attachments so that they can use framebuffer compression.
* Invalidating transient attachments to skip writing to memory.
* Using inline multi-sample resolve to skip writing the multi-sampled data to memory.

sections.name: Tiling
sections.longDescription:
The tiler hardware orchestrates vertex shading and bins primitives into the tile lists read during fragment shading.
Performance counters in this section show how the tiler processes the binning phase vertex and primitive workload.
This GPU uses deferred vertex shading, so the binning phase vertex shading tracked by the tiler performance counters includes only the position shader. Varying shading is deferred until the main phase of render pass processing for most draw calls.

groups.name: Tiler Cycles
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of cycles when individual sub-units inside the tiler are active.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the tiler has position shading requests outstanding.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments every clock cycle when the tiler has an outstanding position shading request that is still being processed by a shader core.

groups.name: Tiler Stall Cycles
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of cycles when individual sub-units inside the tiler are stalled.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the tiler has a stalled position shading buffer.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments every clock cycle when the tiler has a position shading request that it can not send to a shader core because the position buffer is full.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the tiler has a stalled position shading request.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments every clock cycle when the tiler has a position shading request that it can not send to a shader core because the shading request queue is full.

metrics.humanName: Tiler primitive assembly position shading stall cycles
metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when primitive assembly is waiting for position shading.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments every clock cycle when the late primitive assembly stage is waiting for a position shading request to complete.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the tiler has a stalled varying shading request.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments every clock cycle when the tiler has a varying shading request that it can not send to a shader core because the shading request queue is full.

metrics.humanName: Tiler vertex cache read stall cycles
metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when the tiler is stalled waiting for vertex data.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments every clock cycle when an index is ready to be sent to primitive assembly, but its position data is not ready.

groups.name: Tiler Vertex Cache
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of accesses made into the vertex position and varying post-transform caches.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of position lookups that result in a hit in the vertex cache.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments every time a vertex position lookup hits in the vertex cache.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of varying lookups that result in a hit in the vertex cache.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments every time a vertex varying lookup results in a successful hit in the vertex cache.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of varying lookups that miss in the vertex cache.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments every time a vertex varying lookup misses in the vertex cache. Cache misses at this stage result in a varying shading request, although a single request can produce data to handle multiple cache misses.

groups.name: Tiler L2 Reads
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of tiler read accesses from the L2 memory system.

metrics.humanName: Tiler read beats from the L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The number of tiler internal bus data read beats.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every data read cycle the tiler uses on the internal bus from the L2 memory system.

groups.name: Tiler L2 Writes
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of tiler write accesses to the L2 memory system.

metrics.humanName: Tiler write beats to L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The number of internal bus data write beats made by the tiler.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every data write cycle the tiler uses on the internal bus to the L2 memory system.

metrics.humanName: Tiler port 0 write beats to L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The number of internal bus data write beats made by the tiler on port 0.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every data write cycle the tiler uses on port zero to the internal bus to the L2 memory system.

metrics.humanName: Tiler port 1 write beats to L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The number of internal bus data write beats made by the tiler on port 1.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every data write cycle the tiler uses on port one to the internal bus to the L2 memory system.

groups.name: Tiler L2 Read Bytes
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the tiler read bandwidth from the L2 memory system.

metrics.humanName: Tiler read bytes from the L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The number of tiler internal bus data read bytes.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the number of bytes that the tiler reads from the internal bus to the L2 memory system.

groups.name: Tiler L2 Write Bytes
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the tiler write bandwidth to the L2 memory system.

metrics.humanName: Tiler write bytes to L2 memory system
metrics.shortDescription: The number of internal bus data bytes written by the tiler.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the number of bytes that the tiler writes to the internal bus to the L2 memory system.

groups.name: Tiler Shading Requests
groups.longDescription:
This counter group tracks the number of shading requests that are made by the tiler when processing vertex shaders during binning.
Application vertex shaders are split into two pieces, a position shader that computes the vertex position, and a varying shader that computes the remaining vertex shader outputs. The varying shader is only run if a group contains visible vertices that survive primitive culling.
This GPU uses deferred vertex shading and does not run the varying shader for all primitives in the binning phase.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of position shading requests in the tiler geometry flow.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every position shading request in the tiler geometry flow. Position shading runs the first part of the vertex shader, computing the position required to perform clipping and culling. A vertex that is evicted from the post-transform cache must be reshaded if used again, so your index buffers must have good spatial locality of index reuse.
Each request contains {{C::MaliGPUGeomTaskSize.equation}} vertices.
Note that not all types of draw call use this tiler workflow, so this counter might not account for all submitted geometry.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of varying shading requests in the tiler geometry flow.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every varying shading request in the tiler geometry flow. Varying shading runs the second part of the vertex shader, for any primitive that survives clipping and culling. The same vertex is shaded multiple times if it is evicted from the post-transform cache before reuse occurs. Keep good spatial locality of index reuse in your index buffers.
Each request contains {{C::MaliGPUGeomTaskSize.equation}} vertices.
Note that not all types of draw call use this tiler workflow, so this counter might not account for all submitted geometry.

groups.name: Vertex Cache Hit Rate
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the hit rate in the tiler post-transform caches.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage hit rate of the tiler varying cache.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the percentage hit rate of the tiler varying cache used for the index-driven vertex shading pipeline.

sections.name: Internal Memory System
sections.longDescription:
The GPU internal memory interface connects the processing units, such as the shader cores and the tiler, to the GPU L2 cache.
Performance counters in this section show reads and writes into the L2 cache and how the cache responds to them.

groups.name: L2 Cache Requests
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the total number of requests made into the L2 cache from any source.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of L2 cache read requests from internal requesters.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read request received by the L2 cache from an internal requester.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of L2 cache write requests from internal requesters.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every write request received by the L2 cache from an internal requester.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of L2 snoop requests from internal requesters.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every coherency snoop request received by the L2 cache from internal requesters.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of L2 cache line clean unique requests from internal requesters.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every line clean unique request received by the L2 cache from an internal requester.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of L2 cache line evict requests from internal requesters.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every line evict request received by the L2 cache from an internal requester.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of L1 cache read requests sent by the L2 cache to an internal requester.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every L1 cache read request or read response sent by the L2 cache to an internal requester.
Read requests are triggered by a snoop request from one requester that needs data from another requester's L1 to resolve.
Read responses are standard responses back to a requester in response to its own read requests.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of L1 cache write responses sent by the L2 cache to an internal requester.
metrics.longDescription:
This counter increments for every L1 cache write response sent by the L2 cache to an internal requester.
Write responses are standard responses back to a requester in response to its own write requests.

groups.name: L2 Cache Lookups
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the total number of lookups made into the L2 cache from any source.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of L2 cache lookups performed.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every L2 cache lookup made, including all reads, writes, coherency snoops, and cache flush operations.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of L2 cache read lookups performed.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every L2 cache read lookup made.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of L2 cache write lookups performed.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every L2 cache write lookup made.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of coherency snoop lookups triggered by an external requester.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every coherency snoop lookup performed that is triggered by a requester outside of the GPU.

groups.name: L2 Cache Stall Cycles
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the total number of stall cycles that impact L2 cache lookups.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles L2 cache read requests from internal requesters are stalled.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every clock cycle an L2 cache read request from an internal requester is stalled.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when L2 cache write requests from internal requesters are stalled.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every clock cycle when an L2 cache write request from an internal requester is stalled.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when L2 cache snoop requests from internal requesters are stalled.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every clock cycle when an L2 cache coherency snoop request from an internal requester is stalled.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cycles when L1 cache read requests sent by the L2 cache to an internal requester are stalled.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every clock cycle when L1 cache read requests and responses sent by the L2 cache to an internal requester are stalled.

groups.name: L2 Cache Hit Rate
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the hit rate in the L2 cache.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage of internal L2 cache reads that do not result in an external read.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the percentage of internal L2 cache reads that do not result in an external read.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage of internal L2 cache writes that do not result in an external write.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the percentage of internal L2 cache writes that do not result in an external write.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage of internal L2 cache reads that result in an external read.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the percentage of internal L2 cache reads that result in an external read.

metrics.shortDescription: The percentage of internal L2 cache writes that result in an external write.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the percentage of internal L2 cache writes that result in an external write.

groups.name: MMU Hit Rate
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the hit rate in the TLB used for page table lookups handled by the GPU MMU.

metrics.humanName: MMU level 2 lookup TLB hit rate
metrics.shortDescription: The percentage hit rate of the TLB for level 2 table walks.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the percentage hit rate of the main MMU TLB for level 2 table walks.

metrics.humanName: MMU level 3 lookup TLB hit rate
metrics.shortDescription: The percentage hit rate of the TLB for level 3 table walks.
metrics.longDescription: This expression defines the percentage hit rate of the main MMU TLB for level 3 table walks.

groups.name: MMU Translations
groups.longDescription: This counter group shows the number of page table lookups handled by the GPU MMU.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of main MMU address translations performed.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every address lookup made by the main GPU MMU. Increments only occur if all lookups into a local TLB miss.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of level 2 translation table lookups that hit in the main MMU TLB.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read of a level 2 MMU translation table entry that results in a successful hit in the main MMU's TLB.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of level 3 translation table lookups that hit in the main MMU TLB.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every read of a level 3 MMU translation table entry that results in a successful hit in the main MMU's TLB.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of level 2 translation table lookup misses.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every TLB miss that results in a read of a level 2 MMU translation table entry. Table entries each cover 2MB of address space.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of level 3 translation table lookup misses.
metrics.longDescription: This counter increments for every TLB miss that results in a read of a level 3 MMU translation table entry. Table entries each cover 4KB of address space.

sections.name: Constants
sections.longDescription:
Arm GPUs are configurable, with variable performance across products, and variable configurations across devices.
This section lists useful symbolic configuration and constant values that can be used in expressions to compute derived counters. Note that configuration values must be provided by a runtime tool that can query the actual implementation configuration of the target device.

groups.name: Implementation Configuration
groups.longDescription: This constants group contains symbolic constants that define the configuration of a particular device. These must be populated by the counter sampling runtime tooling.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of shader cores implemented in the design.
metrics.longDescription: This configuration constant defines the number of shader cores in the design.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of cache slices implemented in the design.
metrics.longDescription: This configuration constant defines the number of L2 cache slices in the design.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of bytes transferred per external bus beat.
metrics.longDescription: This configuration constant defines the number of bytes transferred per external bus beat.

groups.name: Static Configuration
groups.longDescription: This constants group contains literal constants that define the static configuration and performance characteristics of this product.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of pixels per main phase queue task.
metrics.longDescription: This constant defines the number of pixels in each axis per main phase queue task.

metrics.shortDescription: The size of a block of sequential vertices that the tiler can process concurrently, in each task it issues to the shader cores.
metrics.longDescription: This constant defines the number of threads per vertex shading task issued by the tiler, to perform position shading or varying shading concurrently, for multiple sequential vertices.

metrics.shortDescription: The maximum size of a tile.
metrics.longDescription: This constant defines the size of a tile.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of bits of color storage per pixel available at full tile size.
metrics.longDescription: This constant defines the number of bits of color storage per pixel available when using a {{C::MaliGPUTileSize.equation}} x {{C::MaliGPUTileSize.equation}} tile size. If you use more storage than the available storage for multi-sampling, wide color formats, or multiple render targets, the driver dynamically reduces the tile size until sufficient storage is available.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of threads in a single warp.
metrics.longDescription: This constant defines the number of threads in a single warp.

metrics.shortDescription: The maximum number of concurrent threads in a single core.
metrics.longDescription: This constant defines the maximum number of concurrent threads in a single core. If this product is configurable, this value shows the largest configuration size.

metrics.shortDescription: The number of varying issues per cycle.
metrics.longDescription:
This constant defines the maximum number of varying unit issues that can be made per cycle.
The width of an issue is GPU-dependent.

metrics.shortDescription: The maximum number of texture samples per cycle.
metrics.longDescription: This constant defines the maximum number of texture samples that can be made per cycle.

metrics.shortDescription: The minimum number of cycles needed per texture sample.
metrics.longDescription: This constant defines the minimum number of cycles needed to make a texture sample.

metrics.humanName: Internal shader core bus beat size
metrics.shortDescription: The number of bytes transferred per internal shader core bus beat.
metrics.longDescription: This constant defines the number of bytes transferred per internal shader core bus beat.
metrics.layoutName: Internal shader core bus beat size

metrics.shortDescription: The number of bytes transferred per internal tiler bus beat.
metrics.longDescription: This constant defines the number of bytes transferred per internal tiler bus beat.
